Tequila Tipples for Mexican Independence Day

By Vicki Cruz


Each year on September 16th, Mexico celebrates its independence with plenty of festive parades, parties, food and, of course, tequila!

Make a toast to Mexico’s Independence by mixing up one of these delicious tequila tipples. Salud!

Mexican Martini

Photo Courtesy of El Original


Mexican Martini

Courtesy of Garrett Flanagan for El Original

Ingredients:

 * 1 1/2 oz. Lime Juice
 * 1 1/2 oz. Simple Syrup
 * 3 oz. Tequila
 * 1/2 oz. Olive Juice
 * Olives

Preparation: Shake all ingredients with ice, pour into martini glass, garnish with olives and enjoy!

----------------------------------------

Agua Verde Margarita

Photo Courtesy of Milagro Tequila


Agua Verde (Margarita)

Ingredients:

 * 1 1/2 oz. Milagro Silver
 * 1/4 oz. Avocado
 * 3 Cucumber Slices
 * 1 oz. Fresh Lime Juice
 * 3/4 oz. Agave Nectar
 * Lime Wheel (for Garnish)

Preparation: Combine ingredients and blend with one cup of ice. Pour into a rocks glass. Garnish with a lime wheel.

----------------------------------------

In Love with the Coconut

Photo Courtesy of Milagro Tequila


In Love with Coconut

Ingredients:

 * 1 1/2 oz. Milagro Silver
 * 1/2 oz. Ancho Reyes
 * 3/4 oz. Fresh Lime Juice
 * 1/2 oz. Coconut Syrup (Monin)
 * 2 oz. Ginger Beer (to Top)
 * Toasted Coconut (for Garnish)

Preparation: Combine all ingredients (except ginger beer) in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until cold. Strain into a coconut rimmed rocks glass over fresh ice, top with ginger beer and enjoy.

----------------------------------------

The Freshest Sangria

Photo Courtesy of Milagro Tequila


The Freshest Sangria

Ingredients:

 * 4 oz. Milagro Silver
 * 4 oz. Fresh Lime Juice
 * 4 oz. Grapefruit Juice
 * 8 oz. Grenadine
 * 3 Serrano Peppers

Preparation: In four shooter glasses, pour Milagro Silver neat. Cut serrano peppers in half and remove veins, seeds and stems. Blend the halves with remaining ingredients and allow this pepper infusion to steep for 2-3 hours. Strain and pour into four separate shooter glasses.

----------------------------------------

The Marguerite

Photo Courtesy of 1800 Tequila


The Marguerite

Ingredients:

 * 1 1/2 oz. 1800 Reposado
 * 1 oz. Fresh Squeezed Grapefruit Juice
 * 1/2 oz. Fino Sherry
 * 1/2 oz. Maraschino Liqueur
 * Soda Water (to Top)
 * Grapefruit Twist (for Garnish)

Preparation: Shake all ingredients (except soda water) with ice and strain into an ice-filled Old Fashioned glass. Top with soda water and garnish with a grapefruit twist.

Cinco de Mayo!

Ray Foley


Ray Foley

Published May 4, 2016

Cinco de Mayo!

The Mexican martini was born in the late 70’s when a bartender at Cedar Door Restaurant in Austin, was served a margarita in a martini glass on a trip to Mexico. She returned to Texas raving about the drink, and Cedar Door created its own version, adding in olives.The Mexican martini has since become a Tex-Mex staple and the signature drink of Austin. It comes in many forms: some bartenders are certain it should be served in a shaker, while others serve the drink as a classic martini, but with tequila instead of gin or vodka. Some don’t make the drink without adding olive brine or muddling olives and peppers.This cocktail is hard to find outside of Austin, but is featured at the newly opened authentic Tex-Mex cantina El Original in New York City. If you’d like to make this drink at home, the recipe is below.

Mexican Martini Recipe developed by Garrett Flanagan for El Original
· 3 oz. Your Favorite Tequila
· 1.5 oz. Lime Juice
· 1.5 oz. Simple Syrup
· 0.5 oz. Olive Juice
Shake with ice, pour into martini glass, garnish with olives and enjoy!

Cocktail O’Clock: Olives + Tequila? -

We’re big fans of dirty martinis here at Endless Simmer, not to mention pickle-tinis, and pretty much any other way to salty up a cocktail. What we’d never heard of before was an olive-and-tequila concoction.

With National Tequila Day just around the corner (July 24, as you surely know), it’s about time to take a look at the Mexican martini.

This Austin, Texas speciality comes to us by way of Tex-Mex cantina El Original in New York City and we have to say this one looks worth trying.


Mexican Martini 

Recipe by Garrett Flanagan for El Original

 * 1.5 oz. Lime Juice
 * 1.5 oz. Simple Syrup
 * 3 oz. Tequila
 * 0.5 oz. Olive Juice

Shake with ice, pour into martini glass, garnish with olives and enjoy!

webpage.text:
Mexican Martini Recipe

By Jump to Recipe

Skip the airfare and serve south-of-the-border party fare with this quick and easy cocktail recipe!


I’ve never been to Mexico—but I’ve savored many a Tex-Mex dish here in the States! So it may be surprising to learn that I am not a fan of margaritas. The frozen versions are way too sweet for me, and I just never really warmed up to the more traditional rocks version.

This Mexican martini recipe, on the other hand, perfectly suits my Southwestern tastes! The orange flavors from the Cointreau and orange juice lay a lightly sweet foundation for the subtle herbal tones and whisper of pepper in good-quality tequila. The sweet-and-sour mix plays off the bright citrusy zest of the lime juice, and the lemon-lime soda adds a splash of fizzy fun to bring it all together.

Whether you craft each martini separately with a flourish of bartender magic or stir up a pitcher of them ahead of time, your guests will love how this drink takes margarita-like flavors to a more upscale level.


My tips for next-level martinis

 * Opt for a high-quality tequila, ideally a smooth silver or mellow reposado, to highlight agave nuances and minimize harshness.
 * Chill your martini glasses ahead of time for a sophisticated presentation that helps keep drinks cool.
 * Add a splash of olive brine to the shaker for extra savory depth—a hallmark of classic Austin-style martinis.
 * Make homemade sweet-and-sour mix with equal parts freshly squeezed lemon and lime juice, plus agave nectar to taste. Typically, it’s a one-to-one ratio with the citrus, but slightly less could suffice, since agave is sweeter than sugar.
 * Garnish your drinks with sliced jalapeños for added on-theme spiciness.
 * Sub in blood orange juice for vividly dramatic crimson color and sweeter, berry-like flavors.


How do I store leftovers?

Store leftover Mexican martinis in a well-sealed container in the fridge for up to 24 hours. The flavors of citrus juice and sweet-and-sour mix can quickly change after a day. For party prep, you can scale up and mix the base ingredients—tequila, Cointreau, lime juice, sweet-and-sour mix, and orange juice—in a pitcher, then chill it in the fridge for a few hours. Add the lemon-lime soda and garnishes just before serving so the drink stays fresh and lively. This beverage does not freeze well.


Serving suggestions

Serve your Mexican martinis alongside a full spread of dishes inspired by the flavors of Mexico. If it’s a finger-food party, go for Mexican Stuffed Peppers, Mexican Sushi Roll, and these gorgeous Mexican Molletes. For a sit-down dinner, consider a Chicken Mexican Rice Casserole paired with a vibrant Mexican Chopped Salad and Sopapillas for dessert.

Prep: 5 minutes

Total: 5 minutes

 * 2 ounces silver tequila
 * 1 ounce Cointreau or any orange-flavored liqueur
 * 1 ounce fresh lime juice
 * 1 1/2 ounces sweet-and-sour mix
 * Splash of orange juice
 * Splash of lemon-lime soda
 * Lime wedges and olives optional, for garnish

 * Combine the tequila, orange liqueur, lime juice, sweet-and-sour mix, and orange juice in a cocktail shaker with a handful of ice cubes.
   
   

 * Cover and shake vigorously until the shaker feels cold, about 15 seconds.

 * Strain the mixture into a chilled martini glass.
   
   

 * Add a splash of lemon-lime soda to the drink.

 * Garnish with a lime wedge and one or more olives as desired. Serve immediately.

webpage.text:
Drankjes | Koude en warme dranken om zelf te maken

Koffie recepten

Ben jij gek op koffie? Dan ben je hier op de juiste plek! Wij houden van koffie en delen graag onze lekkerste koffierecepten met je. Of het nu gaat om een koud ijskoffie recept Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad in de zomer of een warme Chai koffie latte Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad of caramel latte machiato Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad in de winter, wij weten zeker dat je ze heerlijk zult vinden. Het Dalgona koffie Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad recept is trouwens ook een grote favoriet hier thuis…


Gezonde dranken

Zelf gezonde drankjes maken is niet alleen leuk, maar ook heel goed voor je. Begin je dag met een kruidige kurkuma thee Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad vol antioxidanten of bekijk ons citroen gember shot Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad recept voor je dagelijkse weerstands boost. We laten je ook zien hoe je makkelijk zelf amandelmelk kunt maken Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad of een verse gemberthee Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad. Supergezond en heel lekker!


Warme drankjes

In de winter maken we graag warme dranken. Probeer onze zelfgemaakte gemberthee Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad of kurkumathee. En als je echt wilt genieten, maak dan onze warme chocolademelk Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad – eventueel met een scheutje rum Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad voor de liefhebber. Deze warme drankjes zijn perfect voor koude dagen en geven je een heerlijk warm gevoel.


Koude dranken

Als het warm is, kiezen we voor verkoeling. Onze ijskoffie en huisgemaakte ijsthee Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad zijn dan echte favorieten. Heb je een feestje in de zomer? Verras je gasten dan met  cocktails, mocktails Deze link opent in een nieuw tabblad of lekkere en feestelijke sapjes. Of houd het simpel met (bruis)water met ijs, fruit en munt voor een superfrisse koude drank.

Onze recepten zijn voor iedereen die van lekkere drankjes houdt, of je nu het liefst koffie drinkt of iets gezonds wil proberen. Voor elk moment van de dag, het hele jaar door, hebben we goede recepten.
